Disclaimer: The below article is sponsored, and the views in it do not represent those of ZyCrypto. Readers should conduct independent research before taking any actions related to the project mentioned in this piece. This article should not be regarded as investment advice.

Alta, a financial infrastructure company building the foundation for the next generation of global finance, has announced $80 million in total funding — including a $47.5 million Series A round and $32.5 million in previous seed financing. The Series A was led by Index Ventures, with participation from GV (Google Ventures), Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg, and Capital 49.

The timing is deliberate. Alta’s launch comes as regulatory clarity improves and institutional demand for tokenized finance accelerates.

Today’s global financial system remains fragmented and riddled with inefficiency. Moving money across borders can take days, and institutions must hold substantial cash buffers to maintain liquidity across jurisdictions and payment networks. Globally, an estimated $4 trillion sits tied up in prefunded accounts.

Alta is building a more efficient alternative — combining instant settlement with global payment connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury management in a single system.

At the core of Alta’s technology is a new blockchain architecture built on recursive zero-knowledge cryptography. It allows institutions to keep balances, transactions, identities, and compliance policies private — while still cryptographically proving that every transaction meets the required rules.

Designed to operate across assets, chains, and jurisdictions, Alta pairs programmable compliance with the controls and scalability that institutional finance and agentic commerce demand.

Leading financial platform Airwallex has chosen to build on Alta, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain technology. Beyond pay-ins and pay-outs via stablecoins, the collaboration will support connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies.

That reflects Alta’s broader positioning: neutral infrastructure that banks, payment providers, and other financial institutions can all build on.

Alta’s first product is designed to help businesses manage liquidity more efficiently and free up the cash buffers trapped in prefunded accounts. Built on tokenized assets, it enables just-in-time funding and more efficient foreign exchange — and lets businesses move instantly in and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, maximizing the interest earned on otherwise idle capital.

“With the rise of agentic banking and programmable payments, stablecoins are becoming an important vector for settlement. Financial institutions need blockchain infrastructure that is private, neutral, regulated, and connected to global fiat rails. Alta is building exactly that,” said Jack Zhang, Co-Founder of Alta and Co-Founder/CEO of Airwallex. “We’re proud to be an early design partner and help Alta deliver onchain finance at institutional scale.”

Alta’s investors bring together expertise across financial technology, enterprise infrastructure, and blockchain innovation.

“Loong is the sort of technologist you only meet a few times in a career. After a major fintech exit from his first company, he went on to run the largest supercomputing calculation in history at its time, then discovered a cancer drug now in human trials. With Catherine’s exceptional track record of bringing industry leaders to the table and Jack’s understanding of the problem space, this is a team we had to back,” said Jan Hammer, Partner at Index Ventures.

“The Alta founders have successfully built and scaled multi-billion-dollar technology and financial infrastructure businesses, and understand how to de-risk complex institutional execution. We have been impressed with their combination of deep-tech blockchain engineering, institutional go-to-market knowledge, and vision for scale, and we look forward to supporting them in their mission to reimagine financial infrastructure at its core,” said Tom Hulme, Managing Partner at GV.

The new funding will support continued development of Alta’s blockchain infrastructure, the expansion of its institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and the growth of its engineering and compliance teams.

#5269. Nanbeige4.3-33B Ties Qwen3.8-27B on Intelligence Index, but Spends 44% More Output Tokens

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Nanbeige4.3-33B matches Qwen3.8-27B at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index but uses 158K output tokens per task against 110K. Here is what that costs locally.

Two models just posted the same score. One needed 158,000 output tokens per task to get there. The other needed 110,000.

Nanbeige4.3-33B, a dense 33-billion-parameter reasoning model from the foundation model team at BOSS Zhipin, scores 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5. According to Artificial Analysis's evaluation, published November 5, that matches Qwen3.8 27B at its xhigh reasoning setting. The model is open weights under Apache 2.0, accepts text only, and has a 524K-token context window.

Behind the tie sits a gap in effort. Artificial Analysis says Nanbeige used 158K output tokens per Intelligence Index task against 110K for Qwen3.8 27B, about 44% more. That weighted average covers answer and reasoning tokens across all nine v5 evaluations, including agentic tool-use turns. For anyone running these models, tokens translate into time, electricity or money, so the same score doesn't mean the same cost.

The Intelligence Index v5 combines nine evaluations, among them AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode 2.0 and AA-Omniscience. A score of 20 puts Nanbeige well above the 6 of Muse Glimmer, a 30B model in the same comparison. Artificial Analysis also notes that Nanbeige sets a new Pareto-optimal point for Intelligence Index against total parameters, since both it and Qwen3.8 27B are dense models. A larger mixture-of-experts model like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, by contrast, scores 33 while activating only 16B parameters per token.

The model card Nanbeige's lab published on Hugging Face describes the base model, positioned as the flagship teacher for the Nanbeige4.3 series. The lab says it will distill agentic capabilities into smaller models, such as an upcoming 3B version. On base-model benchmarks, the card shows 66.9 on MMLU-Pro against 59.3 for Gemma4-31B-Base. Those figures belong to the base model and are separate from the reasoning model's Intelligence Index result.

The two models reach 20 by different routes. Nanbeige scores 30% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 6% for Qwen, and 16% on the CritPt v2 Hard Subset against 4%. It also edges Qwen on AutomationBench-AA, 53% to 48%.

Elsewhere, it falls behind. On AA-Briefcase v1.1 it scores 1162 Elo against 1391, on FrontierCode 2.0 11% against 15%, and on HLE-Diamond 7% against 15%. The knowledge test tells the most distinctive story. On AA-Omniscience v1.1, Nanbeige scores -4 against Qwen's -6, with an 18% hallucination rate against 29%. Yet it answers only 29% of questions against 43%, declines 71% of them and gets 12% correct against 17%.

For general question answering, Qwen's higher accuracy is the better result.

Output tokens aren't a vanity metric. A reasoning model writes out its thinking as tokens, and every one costs decode time. If both models ran at the same speed on the same hardware, Nanbeige would take about 44% longer to finish a typical task.

Local decoding adds a second factor. Generation is usually limited by memory bandwidth, because each new token requires reading the model's weights, and a 33B dense model reads about 20% more weight data per token than a 27B dense model. Assuming the same quantization and the same memory-bound hardware, those two effects compound to roughly 1.7 times the wall-clock time per task. That figure is a back-of-the-envelope calculation, not a measured result.

Nor is there a hosted alternative to soften the blow. Artificial Analysis lists no confirmed public first-party or third-party APIs for Nanbeige, so unlike Qwen, which is sold per token through Alibaba's API, the cost is the hardware you run it on and the time it takes.

Artificial Analysis describes the model as small enough to run locally on a laptop, which holds true with a caveat. The weights are published in BF16, which at 33 billion parameters means roughly 66 GB, far beyond almost any laptop. At 8-bit, the weights fall to about 33 GB, and at 4-bit to about 17 GB, plus memory for the context cache. A machine with 24 GB of unified memory or more can plausibly hold a 4-bit build, though a long context will push it.

The vendor's own quickstart points the other way. The card's SGLang and vLLM examples both set tensor parallelism across four GPUs, which suggests the reference deployment is a multi-GPU server. Its Transformers example also enables trust_remote_code=True, which runs code from the repository. Reading that code first is the safer move, as is serving the model through vLLM or SGLang instead.

Quantization changes the model, too. The Intelligence Index numbers come from Artificial Analysis's own runs, so a 4-bit local build may score somewhat lower, or generate different token counts, than the version they evaluated.

This release is a clean example of why a headline score isn't enough. Nanbeige delivers Qwen-level results at 33B, with strengths in terminal tasks and physics reasoning and a more cautious answering style. The price for those strengths is length.

Anyone choosing between the two should run both on their own workload and record three numbers: the score on their tasks, output tokens per task and seconds per task on their hardware. For terminal-heavy, agentic work, Nanbeige's profile may justify the longer runs. For knowledge-heavy or latency-sensitive work, Qwen's shorter, more accurate answers look stronger.

Three signals are worth watching next: whether the 3B distilled version keeps the model's strengths, whether other labs report the same token behavior, and whether anyone publishes quantized local benchmarks. Until then, the simplest summary is also the most accurate: same score, different bill.

#5267. XRP Ledger Unveils Fee-Free Quantum-Proof Upgrade as Ripple Races Toward 2028 Security Deadline: Here’s What’s Coming

The XRP Ledger is preparing for a major security overhaul as quantum computing moves from a theoretical concern to a growing priority for the crypto industry. With Ripple targeting 2028 for its post-quantum security transition, developers are now unveiling a proposed quantum-resistant upgrade that promises to protect users against future attacks without introducing additional transaction fees.

The development could mark a significant turning point for the network, raising questions about what exactly is changing, how the upgrade will work, and whether XRP holders will need to do anything before the looming security deadline.

The XRP community has a new development to watch as the XRP Ledger Foundation outlines plans to strengthen the network against future quantum computing risks. The proposed upgrade would introduce quantum-resistant accounts, giving users an additional layer of protection against emerging cryptographic threats while keeping transaction costs unchanged.

Although the feature has yet to be implemented, the proposed upgrade would allow XRP Ledger users to register NIST-approved ML-DSA-44 quantum-resistant signing keys and deactivate their existing authentication keys. This would give accounts an additional layer of protection against potential quantum computing attacks, particularly those whose public keys have already been exposed on the network.

Importantly, users could adopt the enhanced security system without changing how they store, hold, or access their XRP. The concern stems from how transactions are authorized on the network. When users sign transactions through their cryptocurrency wallets, their public keys can become exposed, potentially creating an attack vector if sufficiently advanced quantum computers emerge.

Such technology could eventually undermine existing cryptographic protections, putting accounts with exposed public keys at risk. The XRP Ledger Foundation’s proposed solution is designed to address this vulnerability before quantum computing advances to the point where such attacks become practically achievable.

Beyond the additional protection, the proposal has another notable selling point: affordability. Users would not have to pay higher transaction fees to benefit from the enhanced security. In other words, XRP holders could strengthen their accounts against emerging quantum threats without incurring additional transaction costs, making the proposed upgrade particularly appealing to the community.

Although the upgrade has not yet gone live, the team has outlined its next steps, with a migration study planned for the first half of 2027. The research will explore how existing XRPL accounts can move to the new quantum-resistant security framework, including the transition process and what account holders would need to do to adopt the upgraded protection.

Developers are also addressing discrepancies in how the proposed system generates cryptographic keys across its Python, JavaScript, and server implementations, a necessary step toward ensuring consistent and reliable performance across the network.

As ZyCrypto previously reported, Ripple has outlined a comprehensive four-phase roadmap to make the XRP Ledger, its decentralized Layer-1 blockchain, resistant to potential quantum computing attacks, with full quantum readiness targeted for 2028.

Zcash has set a new high in its network hashrate just days after the NU7 upgrade, which slashed block times by a third to 25 seconds. Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade on November 6, 2026, at block 3,543,405.

Zcash network hashrate: 32.62 GSol/s, up 5.8% in 30 days. ⛏️ An all-time high. https://t.co/1vNROBAvd2

Zcash hashrate refers to the total computing power of all miners on the ZEC network. It is calculated by the current network difficulty, the average block find time set by the cryptocurrency network and/or the effective block find time of the latest blocks.

ZEC got 3x faster following the NU7 upgrade, which launched on November 6, with block times down from 75 to 25 seconds, and the Sprout pool retired, marking a new era for Zcash.

Faster blocks mean more room for shielded transactions. NU7 adds per-block limits: 330 Orchard or Ironwood actions, 300 Sapling inputs and outputs, a shared budget of 330 across pools, and no new Sprout JoinSplits. These limits more than double Orchard protocol throughput while reducing the worst-case sync load a spammer can push onto light wallets by about 37%.

NU7 does not raise Zcash's fixed 21 million cap; halvings will now come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving. NU7 also starts allocating funds for future mining rewards. Some 60% of aggregate transaction fees will flow into a public reserve that pays later mining rewards.

In what comes next after the NU7 upgrade, Zcash developers have proposed cutting block times in a potential NU7.1 upgrade just days after NU7 went live. The proposal would reduce target block times from 25 to 20 seconds, aiming to speed up transaction confirmations and improve user experience and network latency.

#5263. Ethereum (ETH) Gas Estimates Are Broken: Explaining the Fix and the Issue

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum transactions can appear successful, but there might be a problem hiding behind the scenes.

A Geth developer has proposed a fix to the client's gas estimation, according to draft pull request #36084 on GitHub. The patch addresses an issue in the current estimator, which could result in incorrect gas limits due to failed internal calls (calls from one smart contract to another) being ignored.

Although the transaction could still be completed, there is no evidence that the action the user wanted has actually happened.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a smart contract calls another smart contract, catches an error, and then proceeds to a refund, records the failure, or skips an item entirely. Technically, the transaction was successful, but the outcome is different for the user.

This could potentially result in wallets suggesting a gas limit that is enough to finish the transaction, but not enough to complete the work inside it. The developer also noted that EIP-8037 could make this behavior more common, since gas returned from failed internal execution can help fund the fallback.

According to the pull request, the change includes a stricter definition of success for gas estimates. This version of Geth would improve the way it deals with internal failures, counting failed internal calls and contract creations instead of checking only whether the transaction completes.

Even if the transaction completes, the estimate would get rejected if it produces more internal failures than a reference execution with a higher gas limit.

Nonetheless, the developer stressed that an internal call that always fails should not push the estimate higher indefinitely. The reference execution enables the estimator to keep existing failures without allowing additional ones caused by insufficient gas. The proposal also introduces a separate Amsterdam reference, preventing unnecessary increases made purely to access the state gas reservoir.

The developer states that they've replayed 432 mainnet transactions with the new set of rules from the Amsterdam update and that the suggested change fixed 64 out of 67 cases.

The gas limit increased by 4%. 254 additional estimates were unaffected due to the lack of the problem, with 3 cases being undetected.

For regular investors, the proposed change should improve the reliability of wallet estimates and reduce transactions that complete without delivering the intended result, despite introducing higher gas limits in some cases. Luckily, there is no proven link between higher gas limits and higher fees.

#5262. Five Forged Receipts Drained $304.5K From Ankr's Ethereum Bridge Using a 0.0044 ankrETH Deposit

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

SlowMist says five forged receipts with valid signatures let an attacker drain about $304,500 from Ankr's Ethereum bridge using one old Optimism deposit. Here is how the check failed.Every one of the five receipts was signed by the bridge's own trusted signer. Every one pointed to a deposit that had already been paid out.

On November 9, an attacker drained about $304,500 from Ankr's Ethereum cross-chain bridge. According to SlowMist's alert, the attacker built five forged receipts that all referenced a single legitimate Optimism transaction, changing the recipient, the token and the withdrawal amount in each one.

All five carried valid signatures from the bridge's trusted consensus signer.

The reused transaction was tiny: a deposit of about 0.0044 ankrETH made on Optimism on November 3, which SlowMist's analysis says had already been redeemed on Ethereum the same day. Six days later, that one settled deposit was cited five times. The incident is recorded in the SlowMist Hacked database.Blockaid flagged the exploit as it unfolded, at about 08:42 UTC, with roughly $292,000 already gone. SlowMist followed at 09:14 UTC with the higher $304,500 estimate and an explanation of the forged receipts. Ankr paused withdrawals, and no recovery plan has been confirmed.

The design is common across lock-and-release bridges. A user deposits on the source chain, and an off-chain set of signers watches for that deposit and signs a receipt describing it. The destination contract, in this case Ankr's Ethereum bridge contract, checks that the receipt carries a valid signature and then releases the funds.That setup makes the signers the source of truth. The contract can't see Optimism, so it leans on the signature to prove the deposit happened. The weak point sits in the gap between "the signer signed this" and "this really happened." A contract that treats the first as proof of the second inherits every mistake the signing process makes.

SlowMist's finding is precise: the withdrawal function released assets without independently verifying the actual event on the source chain. A signature confirmed that the signer approved a message. It did not confirm that the message matched a deposit that existed, that was still unused, and that involved the same recipient, token and amount.The replay angle deserves attention, even though SlowMist's summary only implies it. A bridge normally marks each source event as consumed, keyed to something fixed like the source chain, transaction hash and log index, so it can be paid out once. If replay protection keys on the contents of the receipt instead, changing the recipient, token or amount produces a receipt the contract has never seen. Five edited receipts against one deposit would then look like five fresh claims. That is one plausible way the pieces fit together, not a finding the researchers have published.Bridge history offers parallels. In 2022, Wormhole lost about $325 million when an attacker got a forged message past its signature verification, and Nomad lost about $190 million after a misconfiguration let nearly any message pass as valid. The Ankr case is smaller, but it shares the same root: the verification step accepted something it shouldn't have.

The Ethereum transactions show the attacker extracted about 82.91 ankrETH, 515,206 ankrPOL and 7.98 million ANKR tokens. Blockaid described the five withdraw calls as using the tiny Optimism deposit to unlock the bridge's locked inventory and send it to a new wallet.The mix of assets tells its own story. Each forged receipt named a different token and amount, which suggests the attacker picked targets based on what the bridge held. That fits receipts built entirely by the attacker, apart from the one real transaction reference. Anyone wanting to trace them can open the bridge contract's transaction list on Etherscan and filter for the five `withdraw` calls on November 9.

The most important fact is still missing. SlowMist says the origin of the unauthorized signatures is under investigation, and it hasn't confirmed whether the signers were compromised.A valid signature on a forged receipt has a short list of explanations. A signing key, or the service holding it, could have been accessed. A signing service could have been tricked into signing attacker-supplied data. Or the signing logic itself could have a flaw that produces signatures for receipts it shouldn't. Each one points to a different fix: a stolen key means rotating signers, a manipulated service means tightening input validation off-chain, and a logic flaw means rewriting the signing rules.Whichever it turns out to be, the on-chain contract and the off-chain signer both failed to ask the same question. Either one verifying the source event would likely have stopped the attack, and neither did.

The lessons are narrow and practical. Replay protection should key on the immutable identity of the source event, not on the receipt's contents, and a source event should be consumable exactly once. The destination contract should confirm that the receipt's recipient, token and amount match what the source-chain event actually recorded, using a proof or an independent verifier instead of trusting the signer alone.Signer infrastructure needs its own scrutiny. Threshold schemes, hardware-backed keys and strict limits on what a signing service will sign all shrink the damage from a single failure. Rate limits and per-withdrawal caps help as well. A bridge that can release its entire locked inventory in five calls has no brake once a signature check is defeated.Trust in a bridge comes in layers, and one layer rarely holds up alone. Users with funds in Ankr's bridge should watch for the project's post-mortem and its plan for restoring withdrawals. For developers, the question to put to their own code is a blunt one: if a signer signs something false, what stops the contract from believing it?

A trader on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, whose wallet was previously linked to the exploit of SocialFi project UXLINK, has started closing $148 million in open positions after suffering heavy losses.

On November 9, the trader launched a 16-hour TWAP algorithm to sell off the positions. The algorithm is set to end by 06:00 GMT on November 10.

The address was previously considered the most profitable one on Hyperliquid. However, the recent market downturn changed that, and the trader is now facing a net loss of $3.3 million.

The trader's Ethereum long position includes 30,282 ETH worth around $55.46 million, with a liquidation price of $1,740.

The trader also holds a 550,000 SOL long with 10x leverage. The position will be fully liquidated if the price of Solana falls to $65.6.

Besides, the trader holds 35.03 million XRP worth around $35 million, with a liquidation price of $0.94.

The selling of these positions is already putting pressure on the prices of all three cryptocurrencies.

In September 2025, UXLINK, a crypto social network with Telegram integration, suffered a hacker attack.

The attackers exploited the project's multisig infrastructure, which allowed them to drain the project's treasury and mint new tokens.

The total damage from the exploit and the subsequent crash of the UXLINK token price was estimated at around $42 million.

In August 2026, an anonymous trader deposited $11.54 million USDC on Hyperliquid.

According to EmberCN, the wallet that was used to pay gas fees for the trader received ETH from addresses that had previously received stolen UXLINK funds.

Since then, the trader has closed five profitable trades with a net gain of $5.71 million.

At the end of October, the trader was still holding $5.6 million in unrealized profit on the Ethereum position.

The recent market downturn erased that profit, and most of the trader's funds are now at risk of liquidation.

#5260. Bitcoin, Gold & Productive Land: Your Shield Against Inflation: Anthony Pompliano

Popular crypto commentator Anthony Pompliano has shortlisted Bitcoin, Gold and Productive land to combat inflation in the uncertain times ahead. He has warned multiple times that the dollarized economy is in decline, and consumers need to protect their wealth by investing in scarce, useful assets that will hold their value well.

He used the term “money printer” in his tweet, which has often been used satirically to attack central banks for their money-printing spree. The short tweet sums up the ethos of the crypto-savvy investor class who have been clamoring for better wealth management for the better part of the last decade and a half. He, along with cypherpunks and other maximalists, believes the best defense against the onslaught of inflationary forces is to invest in assets that cannot be conjured out of thin air.

This is not the first time Pompliano has stated his preference for these three assets. Bitcoin is obviously the asset of choice for this particular demographic that emerged after the devastating 2008 financial crisis.

Gold is obviously another major asset that has withstood the test of time and has appreciated strongly in the last decade or so. Productive land is another asset with a strong future as the world faces uncertain times, with food insecurity at record levels.

The timing of the tweet is crucial, as investors look for orthodox and unorthodox ways to preserve or increase their wealth over time. The effects of large-scale stimulus and debt accumulation cannot be understated. Inflation is reducing the value of savings, and the interest-based economy can hardly keep up with it, let alone deliver a steady net increase.

Twitter responses to the post varied a lot. A large section of Pompliano’s followers said it was a good trio of assets and highlighted their explosive growth over the years. However, others criticized that it wasn’t easy to hold any of these three assets.

Gold requires custody, and holding it individually can be risky, too, with no yield. Bitcoin, on the other hand, requires a relatively tech-savvy mindset and can be volatile at times. Thirdly, land requires management, faces liquidity constraints, and can be affected by local economic or environmental factors. It is not a walk in the park to take advantage of any of these assets.

However, given the uncertain future, they are certainly worth considering, as we all know one thing: fiat is likely to get worse over time.

#5259. Cardano Hits Epoch 666: Why Is It So Significant?

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Cardano (ADA) has entered epoch 666, yet another milestone for the blockchain, which has been live since its launch in September 2017.

The number has drawn attention for its connection to the biblical 666, but the development also points to the Cardano network's basic timekeeping and staking mechanism.

Popular Cardano blockchain explorer Cexplorer displays that epoch 666 started on Nov. 5, 2026, and is expected to end on Nov. 10, with 1 day and 10 hours left to close. The milestone marks another five-day cycle finished in Cardano's long-running proof-of-stake system.

Cardano divides its operation into epochs, which are five days long and consist of 432,000 one-second slots. The importance of epoch 666 is largely symbolic and not technical, as it does not coincide with any major protocol upgrades or hard forks. But the number 666 has merely provided an interesting talking point for the Cardano community.

In a separate milestone, the Cardano network has processed over 127,000,000 transactions on mainnet. According to Cexplorer data, Cardano has recorded a total of 127,203,164 transactions.

In upgrade news, DijkstraNet, the Dijkstra hard fork testnet, has been hard forked to protocol version 12 and is now available for testing and integration against the full Dijkstra feature set, with the exception of Linear Leios.

Node 11.2 was pre-released on October 28 and successfully used to transition DijkstraNet into the Dijkstra era, and DB Sync 13.8.0.0 was released for all networks.

In separate upgrade news, Midnight has completed its upgrade from Ledger 8 to Ledger 9, bringing new capabilities for developers alongside security, compatibility, and performance improvements across the network.

Ledger 9 introduces native support for widely used cryptographic standards including ECDSA and Keccak-256, expands wallet and custody compatibility, and enables contracts to interact directly with one another.

Keccak-256 is the standard algorithm that Ethereum uses to scramble data into fixed-length cryptographic fingerprints. ECDSA is the standard digital signature method that networks like Bitcoin and Ethereum use to prove ownership of a specific wallet address.

Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has shared new metrics on the Gram wallet integration in the messenger.

According to Durov, over the last 48 hours alone, users activated more than 700,000 non-custodial Gram wallets.

The screenshot shared by the Telegram CEO shows more than 329,000 new addresses a day. According to GRAM documentation, a wallet is created automatically when a user receives their first token transfer.

700K+ self-custodial wallets created on Telegram in the last 48 hours alone. Adoption spreads virally: a wallet activates the moment someone receives Grams. The crypto revolution is going strong. https://t.co/JPO2KVMip0

The growth comes after a series of changes Telegram made to the TON network earlier this year under Durov's "Make TON Great Again" campaign.

Back in 2020, Durov was forced to kill the original Telegram Open Network project and return more than $1.2 billion to investors after a lawsuit from the US SEC.

Community developers kept the open-source code alive as The Open Network (Toncoin).

This year, Telegram became the largest validator of the network. Besides, Telegram cut TON fees sixfold.

In June, the token was renamed back to its original name, Gram, after a community vote, with 81% of voters in favor. In July, Durov announced that Telegram would integrate a native non-custodial Gram wallet into every Telegram app.

The Telegram CEO described it as "the largest deployment of a non-custodial crypto wallet in history" and promised instant zero-fee transactions for more than 1 billion Telegram users.

According to TON developer Andrew Rogozov, the custodial Wallet in Telegram will stay separate from the new wallet. Now, onboarding happens natively within standard chat windows.

Still, while wallet creation metrics break records, liquidity inside the network is lagging behind with total value locked at $42.01 million, according to DefiLlama.

These hundreds of thousands of new addresses are mostly making microtransactions, such as buying Telegram Premium, paying for in-app ads, or settling small P2P transfers.

Besides, Telegram's validator weight is raising centralization concerns among industry critics. At the same time, the native wallet is still unavailable for US users.

At press time, Gram is trading at $1.05. The token is still more than 87% below its 2024 high of $8.25.

"The crypto revolution is going strong," Durov said.

Ripple USD (RLUSD) now tops the chart for short-term volume growth on decentralized exchanges (DEXs), outpacing Ethena's USDe. RWA Foundation, citing Token Terminal data, shows RLUSD's DEX trading volume jumped by $127.4 million over the past seven days.

USDe, the synthetic dollar issued by Ethena, has a bigger market cap of $4.97 billion at press time. Its DEX volume grew by $71.4 million, giving RLUSD a $56 million lead for the week.

Other major DeFi stablecoins, Usual's USD0 and Aave's GHO among them, stayed below $20 million.

Ethena offers roughly 5% yield through sUSDe staking. According to Ethena's documentation, the main risk of its delta-neutral model, which relies on short positions in perpetual futures, is prolonged negative funding rates.

USDe supply peaked above $14 billion in 2025. Ethena's fee switch and ENA buybacks are set to start only once the 14-day average USDe supply reaches $7.5 billion.

RLUSD is issued under the supervision of the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) and backed 100% by cash and short-term U.S. Treasuries, with monthly attestations of its reserves.

BNY acts as the custodian of RLUSD reserves.

In late October, the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) gave final approval to Ripple National Trust Bank. The bank will manage RLUSD reserves under federal oversight.

Besides it, RLUSD is available in Spark's Stablecoin FX pool on Uniswap v4, which lets corporate players make multi-million-dollar swaps.

According to RWA Foundation, about 92% of RLUSD turnover on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) runs through direct pairs with XRP.

Ripple also expanded its partnership with Robinhood. According to the companies, Bitstamp will use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for settlement, while Robinhood plans to offer RLUSD to its retail customers by the end of the year.

At the same time, Coinbase added RLUSD to Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and its retail app, with 1:1 USD conversion on the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base.

At press time, RLUSD's market cap stands at $2.69 billion, roughly half USDe's size. The stablecoin started 2026 at about $1.28 billion.

#5255. How Bittensor's Gamma Turns Every AI Payment Into an Alpha Burn

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Paying a Bittensor subnet with gamma burns its alpha token. Here is how gamma gets minted, how the lower-price rule works and why the credit can never be converted back.Pay a Bittensor subnet for an AI answer with gamma, and your payment vanishes. The alpha token behind it gets burned, the credit gets spent, and nobody can redeem either one.

Using a subnet's service today usually means creating an account, adding funds and collecting an API key, and every additional subnet repeats the routine. Opentensor announced gamma to cut that friction. With gamma, a Bittensor wallet handles both access and payment across any subnet that adopts the standard.The mechanics are laid out in the gamma guide in the subtensor docs. Gamma is a credit a subnet can accept as payment, valued in US dollars. A customer gets it by burning that subnet's alpha token, and each dollar of burned alpha value mints one gamma, so a burn valued at $100 creates 100 gamma.Each balance stays tied to the subnet where it was created. Gamma minted for subnet 51 can't pay for a service on any other subnet. Root switches the system on network-wide, and each subnet owner or lease beneficiary then enables it for their own subnet.

Customers have two ways in. They can pay with TAO, and the protocol buys the subnet’s alpha and burns it in a single transaction. Or they can pay with alpha they already hold on that subnet, and the protocol burns it directly to create gamma.

Setup takes four steps. The customer creates a fresh hotkey that will act as an API key, associates it with their coldkey, looks up the service they want and mints. The docs give the command: btcli gamma mint --netuid 51 --hotkey API_KEY --amount-tao 10 --service-hotkey SERVICE_HOTKEY. The TAO route follows the same pool and flow accounting as stake-burn and creates no stake position. Users who hold stake can burn it with mint-gamma-with-stake, and --amount-alpha all burns the whole position.

The gamma lands in a deposit. Each deposit belongs to the minting coldkey and is keyed by the API-key hotkey, which signs the customer's requests. A hotkey holds at most one deposit per subnet, and a coldkey holds at most 64 per subnet. The docs warn against reusing a staking hotkey or a coldkey, because requests signed with the key get paid from the deposit.A few guardrails apply. A mint must reach at least 0.1 gamma. By default, the SDK quotes the mint first and fails it if the result lands more than 5% below the quote. The mint also needs a TAO/USD price no older than 300 blocks, about an hour.

Gamma’s valuation rule decides how much credit a burn buys. The protocol values the burned alpha in TAO, then converts that figure to dollars through an on-chain TAO/USD price feed. The TAO value equals alpha multiplied by the lower of two prices, the gamma price and the spot price, which the docs write as alpha × min(gamma price, spot price).

Every subnet keeps a gamma price. When a subnet registers, the price starts at the median alpha price across subnets. After that it moves asymmetrically. If spot falls, the gamma price falls to match at once. If spot rises, the gamma price climbs slowly toward it, closing a small slice of the gap each block, so the gap halves every 600 blocks, roughly two hours. However high spot jumps, the gamma price can at most double every 600 blocks.An example shows the effect. Say a user burns 100 alpha when spot sits at 0.05 TAO but the gamma price lags at 0.04. The mint uses 0.04, which gives 4 TAO of value, and at $400 per TAO that mints 1,600 gamma. Had the gamma price caught up, the same burn would mint 2,000, so the lag costs the burner 400 gamma. A short-lived pump buys no extra credit. The figures are illustrative, but the rule comes straight from the docs.The TAO/USD feed gets similar damping. A root-controlled oracle supplies the price, and the accepted price falls to a lower feed immediately but rises at most 66 parts per million per block, about 2% an hour. The docs admit the oracle is trusted: its accepted price can climb up to roughly 61% a day until root replaces or removes it.One more detail matters. The docs say alpha is valued at these prices, not at what selling it would return, so a burn that is large relative to the pool is worth more than a sale would be. A big burner gets credit for full value instead of a slipped sale price.Once minted, gamma holds its dollar value whether TAO or alpha prices rise or fall. Service providers still set their own prices.

To use a service, a person or an AI agent signs a request with a hotkey from their Bittensor wallet. The subnet owner, or another authorized account, deducts the required credits from that hotkey's gamma balance before delivering the service. Nothing transfers to anyone. The designated spender calls `spend-gamma` with up to 512 entries per call, each naming a hotkey, an amount and a 32-byte reference, and the spent gamma is destroyed on the spot.The reference doubles as a receipt. By convention it holds the service's own ID for the request being paid, returned with the response, so the customer can match each spend to a specific request. The chain repeats the reference in its events and reads it nowhere else, so an entry sent twice spends twice.Customers keep control throughout. The minting coldkey can set a daily spend cap that refills linearly over 7,200 blocks, about a day, and a cap of zero pauses the deposit. The coldkey can also change the spender, keep separate deposits for different apps and agents, and top up an existing deposit without switching hotkeys. Because the coldkey can pause or redirect at any moment, services spend ahead: they spend what they are about to serve, then serve what was spent. A spender can hand this right to a `GammaSpend` proxy, which can make no other call.Both minting and spending leave public records on-chain, so anyone can audit how much credit a subnet has created and how much customers have used.

The limits are strict. Gamma can't be transferred to another wallet, and it can't be converted back into alpha or TAO. It confers no claim on any party and can't be redeemed. Each subnet chooses whether, and at what prices, it accepts its own gamma.

The docs flag the sharpest risk directly: dissolving or pruning a subnet destroys all of its gamma, and holders receive nothing. A customer who prepaid a large deposit to a subnet that later shuts down loses it. Moving gamma between your own deposits is allowed, and a deposit opened under someone else's hotkey stays yours, since you can pull the gamma back at any time.A coldkey swap adds a few wrinkles. While one is announced, the coldkey's gamma calls are refused, though its spenders keep spending. After a subnet owner swaps coldkeys, deposits that name the old one keep it until the owner republishes its service.

The docs answer the economic question in one sentence: spent gamma pays its spender nothing. The value of the burned alpha accrues to the subnet's alpha holders.

That makes gamma a direct demand mechanism for alpha. Creating gamma always burns the subnet's alpha, which removes those tokens from circulation for good. When customers pay with TAO, the protocol first buys alpha from the subnet's pool, so TAO-funded purchases add buying pressure before the burn. Every dollar of AI usage ties a purchase of service credits to a burn of alpha.

A service operator earns through the alpha it holds and the emissions its subnet receives, not through a payment from customers. The structure rewards subnets that attract real usage, since usage shrinks their alpha supply.Two questions remain open. Customers get dollar-denominated credit, but the burn that funds it follows alpha prices, so heavy usage during a price spike may feel expensive. Holders also carry the dissolution risk, which will push careful buyers toward established subnets. Which services accept gamma, and at what price, will show whether this becomes a real payments layer or a niche tool. The mechanism is clear, and adoption is the unknown.

#5251. North Korean Hackers Flip Stolen Binance Funds Into NEAR Meme Coins

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

North Korea's TraderTraitor group has started laundering funds stolen from Binance through newly created meme tokens, according to Elliptic.

The $6.4 billion Binance hack took place in October 2026 and was attributed to TraderTraitor.

According to Elliptic, the hackers have used this technique on Tron and NEAR, while a similar approach has appeared on Solana.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, 2026, the hackers launched at least six of these tokens on NEAR: FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU. Launching one cost around 25 NEAR (about $90).

According to Elliptic, the hackers paired each token with NEAR in a liquidity pool on a decentralized exchange (DEX). Wallets holding stolen NEAR deposited it into the pool and received the new token. A second set of wallets then sold the token back into the pool and withdrew NEAR.

This way, the funds never move directly from the wallets holding stolen assets to the receiving wallets.

According to Elliptic, the receiving wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit.

Each token got typical meme branding, from monkeys to an image of Elon Musk under an "Elon 2028 President" banner. Elliptic noted that Musk is not linked to the tokens.

Each token was sold for the first time less than three hours after launch, and at least 75% of its trading took place within one day. None of the six tokens has traded since Nov. 8, and the creators of four of them withdrew the remaining liquidity on that day.

In total, 117,000 NEAR (about $421,000) moved through the scheme. Most of it then went into stablecoins or to a cross-chain bridge.

Elliptic noted that five of the six token creators received funds from a wallet that had been selling the previous token 2 to 13 minutes before the new launch, and in this way the operation funded itself.

The only outside activity was a few small purchases of FUK on its first day, which accounted for less than 1% of its volume, Elliptic said.

According to Elliptic, the on-chain trail stays public, and the technique makes tracing the funds slower. The hackers can also create many tokens and abandon each one after use.

In 2025, after the Bybit hack, the same scheme moved at least $24 million through Tron. In that case, the hackers paired a worthless token with a stablecoin.

In the Binance case, Elliptic identified a similar token on Tron on Nov. 2. On Nov. 3, stolen SOL was swapped into existing thinly traded tokens on Solana and then sold for USDC.

Elliptic said that so far only a small part of the stolen funds has gone through meme tokens. About 11.8 million NEAR from the theft has not moved yet, and at press time, NEAR is trading at $3.60, which puts these funds at around $42.4 million.

Elliptic also advises compliance teams to check funds coming from liquidity pools, especially pools with newly created tokens.

"Laundering is a race to move funds before they are flagged," Elliptic added.

#5247. Bitcoin Slides to $73,510 Over the Weekend: Did Nvidia Scandal Trigger BTC’s $2,000 Flash Crash?

Bitcoin news: BTC fell to $73,510 on Sunday, 100 minutes after the Nvidia scandal broke. Thin weekend trading let the drop run further.

In Bitcoin news overnight, BTC USD price fell from $75,607 to $73,510 in ten minutes on Sunday evening, its lowest price since August 21. The worst of it came at 21:55 UTC, or 4:55 p.m. in New York. In that single minute, Bitcoin dropped 1.9% on Binance.

Most traders blamed Nvidia. Earlier that afternoon, CNBC reported that Nvidia’s board had opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was passing information to Beijing (it’s just speculation for now).

Huang admitted the affair in an email to staff.

After Jensen Huang admitted having an affair, a whale opened a 10x short on 30,000 $NVDA ($5.44M) on Hyperliquid.https://t.co/RztJx5FNge pic.twitter.com/zuyV2K0ftN

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 9, 2026

The bounce since then has been small. BTC traded at $74,184 on Binance on Monday morning, 2.2% below where it stood when the Nvidia story broke. The drop also marked a fifth straight losing week: the weekly candle closed at $74,851, below the week’s open of $78,354.

So did the Nvidia scandal really trigger the dump, or did thin weekend trading turn an ordinary sell-off into a sharp one?

Discover: Sam Altman ChatGPT AI Predicts an Insane Move for Cardano (ADA)

The timing does not fit a straight reaction to the news. CNBC published its report at 3:12 p.m. Eastern time on Sunday, which is 20:12 UTC. Bitcoin traded at $75,880 on Binance in that minute. For the next 90 minutes, almost nothing happened. At 21:44 UTC, BTC sat at $75,607, just 0.4% lower than when the story appeared.

Then the selling started, and it started in Ethereum. Between 21:50 and 21:55 UTC, ETH fell 6.9% on Binance, from $2,213 to $2,060. Bitcoin fell 2.4% over the same five minutes.

That pattern points to a liquidation cascade, a chain of forced sales. Traders who borrow to bet on higher prices get their positions force-closed when the price falls past a set point. Each forced sale pushes the price down to the next group of bets.

BREAKING: $1,000,000,000 liquidated from the crypto market in the past 10 minutes.$BTC falls under $74,000$ETH falls under $2,125$XRP falls under $1.10 $SOL falls under $90 pic.twitter.com/hIZhzQFJJe

— Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru) November 8, 2026

The news still mattered. Nvidia is the biggest AI stock, and Bitcoin has traded in step with AI shares for weeks: Thursday’s chip-stock sell-off is what pushed BTC below its 200-day average. With stock markets closed, crypto was the only market open to sell into the headline.

A second headline added to the Bitcoin news mood. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Iran’s demands “outrageous” and said talks had made no progress.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Weekend trading explains why the drop went so far. Over the past year, about $24 million of BTC changed hands on Binance in a typical weekend hour, half the $48 million in a typical weekday hour.

We checked every hour in that year in which Bitcoin fell at least 2.5% below the hour’s opening price. There were 29 of them.

Sunday’s drop came with $180 million of trading in the hour. That is the second-lowest of all 29, and about half the median of $366 million.

In other words, it took less selling than usual to move the price this far. The busiest minute, 21:55 UTC, traded $75 million of BTC on Binance, about three times what changes hands in a whole weekend hour.

Weekends do not cause more crashes, though. Only 6 of the 29 drops came on a Saturday or Sunday, slightly fewer than the 29% of all hours that fall on weekends. What a quiet weekend changes is how far the price moves for each dollar sold.

One note: much of the forced selling happens in futures markets, which this count does not include.

So both played a part. Nvidia and Iran gave traders a reason to cut risk, and thin weekend trading let the selling run further than it would on a weekday.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

It held on the first test. BTC bounced to $75,735 within two hours of the low, but it has slipped back to $74,184, and the daily chart still leans lower.

Bitcoin trades below all three of its daily exponential moving averages (EMAs), trend lines that give recent prices more weight. It lost the 200-day EMA, which tracks the long-term trend, on Thursday.

For traders following Bitcoin news this week, Monday’s stock market open is the next test. It is the first chance for Nvidia shares to trade on the news, eight days before the company reports earnings on November 17.

#5245. Charles Schwab Expands Crypto Trading to SOL, AVAX and LINK, XRP Not Included

American brokerage giant Charles Schwab has announced that it is expanding its crypto trading platform, Schwab Crypto, with the addition of Solana (SOL), Avalanche (AVAX) and Chainlink (LINK) for trading.

The three new coins expand the existing list of two cryptocurrencies, Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), that can be traded directly. This now means that users can trade five cryptocurrencies directly on the platform.

Notably, however, XRP, one of the largest cryptocurrencies by market cap, is still missing from the list of available coins.

In its official press release, Schwab's head of digital assets, Joe Vietri, underlined the brokerage's commitment to further expanding its crypto trading options.

Also, the company confirmed that it will be adding more cryptocurrencies and digital assets going forward. But it didn't specify whether this includes XRP.

Although XRP is not offered directly on the Schwab Crypto trading platform, it is still available to Schwab users in one way or another.

Charles Schwab offers standard and micro futures contracts on XRP through its thinkorswim platform.

In July 2025, the company pointed out the availability of XRP futures with the ticker /XRP and also smaller micro contracts with the ticker /MXP.

It further expanded its derivatives trading platform with the addition of almost 24/7 trading for certain crypto futures, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP, in June 2026.

Charles Schwab's aggressive approach to the crypto industry has been noticeable throughout 2026.

First, the company officially announced Schwab Crypto on April 16. In this announcement, it outlined its plans to introduce direct trading of Bitcoin and Ethereum for retail users.

The next major development came on Oct. 15, when Rick Wurster, the CEO of Charles Schwab, confirmed the introduction of crypto transfers.

The platform now allows eligible customers to transfer eligible crypto assets to and from external wallets through the Schwab Crypto platform. However, this is not yet available to all customers. Access is being rolled out gradually.

The recent US stock market decline has pushed several stock prices lower. However, some companies have continued to report higher revenue and profits despite the market fall. This has raised interest in stocks that have dropped sharply from their recent highs but continue to show business growth.Here is why each stock has come under pressure and what investors should watch.

Nvidia shares have fallen 26.6% from their October 6 high as investors pulled back from AI stocks following the US midterm elections. Concerns over new data centre rules and reports involving CEO Jensen Huang and a woman suspected of sharing information with China added to the pressure.

However, Nvidia’s business remains strong. Its revenue more than doubled year over year, while profit grew 126%. The company continues to supply AI chips to major technology companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Google.

The stock is now trading at its lowest valuation based on past earnings since May 2019. Its November 17 earnings report will be an important event for investors.

Applied Digital builds and operates data centres for AI companies. Its shares have dropped around 74% from their May high of $50.72, recently reaching $13.11. The decline comes amid concerns about AI spending, data centre expansion and opposition to new data centre projects in the US.

However, the company has signed leases for approximately 1.4 gigawatts of capacity, while only 250 megawatts are currently operational. This means much of its planned capacity is yet to generate revenue.

Revenue has grown more than fourfold from a year ago. Management expects 300 megawatts of capacity to be operational in North Dakota by the end of 2026.

Investors will be watching whether the company can complete its projects on time and turn signed leases into revenue.

Microchip Technology makes chips used in cars, home appliances, industrial equipment, defence systems and data centres.

Its shares dropped 22.6% in two days after the company gave a weak outlook for the next quarter. Management said some sales recorded in September were one-time orders and would not repeat.

Despite the decline, the analysis points to a significant improvement in profitability. Daily profit reportedly increased from around $450,000 a year ago to $4.4 million.

Historical data also shows that the stock recovered within a year after eight previous declines of more than 40% from its record highs. However, it often fell further before recovering, so another decline remains possible.

Reddit shares fell 29% on October 30 after its latest earnings report raised concerns about user growth in the US.

Daily active users in the country declined from 53.2 million to 50.7 million. Google’s AI-powered search results are also creating concerns that fewer people will visit Reddit through search.

However, Reddit’s global daily active users increased 12% to 130.3 million. Revenue grew 53% to $895 million, while profit increased 74% to $283 million.

The company expects holiday-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, compared with $726 million a year earlier.

Despite the recent fall, Reddit shares look attractive because of its revenue growth, profitability and relatively low debt.

SoFi offers banking, personal loans, credit cards, savings accounts and investment services through a single digital platform.

The company added a record 1.2 million members last quarter, taking its total membership to 17.1 million, up 35% from a year ago. Revenue increased 44% to $1.4 billion, while profit rose from $139 million to $241 million.

However, the stock has lost nearly half its value since reaching $32.73 in November 2025. Rising interest rates, pressure on banking stocks and concerns about its technology business have contributed to the decline.

This can be a possible buying opportunity because SoFi’s customer base and profits continue to grow despite the falling share price. A move above $17.74 could also indicate improving momentum.

All five stocks have fallen sharply, but their recovery will depend on different factors. Nvidia’s upcoming earnings, Applied Digital’s data centre expansion, Reddit’s user growth, SoFi’s profitability and Microchip’s next business outlook will be important developments.

#5243. Ripple's Schwartz Debunks XRP Price Myth

David Schwartz, the former chief technology officer at Ripple and one of the creators of the XRP Ledger (XRPL), has dispelled one of the most common myths regarding the key factors that could impact the price of XRP.

The former Ripple CTO took to the X social media platform to challenge the idea that the use of XRP as the native gas token of the XRP Ledger could be a major factor in determining the price of the cryptocurrency.

"I don't think anybody who knows anything has said that the use of XRP as gas will be a major driver of the price of XRP," Schwartz wrote.

The comment was made as the Ripple veteran took part in the ever-growing debate centered around the poor price performance of XRP and the place of the cryptocurrency in Ripple's ever-expanding ecosystem.

The former Ripple CTO directed the audience's attention to a post from November 2025, in which he explained his thoughts on how mass adoption of the XRP Ledger could lead to greater value for the ledger's native cryptocurrency.

"The increased use and adoption of XRPL will add value to XRP by its privileged place on the ledger," Schwartz said.

He emphasized that XRP has several unique properties, including the lack of counterparty risk, the fact that it's jurisdictionless, and its privileged place in the network's autobridging features.

In addition, Schwartz argued that it would be hard to imagine the XRP Ledger succeeding on a mass scale without XRP capturing a significant portion of the value created by such success.

"I really do think it's hard to think we could end up in a world where XRPL is successful and XRP doesn't get a good fraction of that value," he said.

Nevertheless, Schwartz also said earlier that the XRP Ledger was not created with the sole intent of pushing the price of XRP higher. Instead, the original goal was to create a fast and cheap payment system with a native digital asset and a decentralized exchange feature.

Schwartz's recent comments come as frustration among XRP holders over the poor performance of the cryptocurrency is on the rise.

As of Monday, the Ripple-related token was trading at around the $1.09 level, down more than 12% in the last seven days.

Recently, Schwartz admitted that his influence on the market price of XRP is very small.

"Do I have anything to do with the price of XRP? Honestly? I guess probably not anything. But very little," he wrote during another interaction with critics.

#5242. Vitalik Buterin Backs an AI Slowdown as AI Tokens Slide 30%: Is the AI Crypto Bubble Popping?

Vitalik Buterin backs slowing the AI data center race. AI tokens fell 29.7% in 30 days, three times Bitcoin. Is the AI crypto bubble popping?

Vitalik Buterin said on Sunday that slowing the AI data center race is probably a good thing, as the crypto bubble around AI tokens loses air. The Ethereum co-founder made the case in a post on X.

He pushed back on what he called the “strong emotional reaction” against the anti-data-center movement.

I know this is a predictable opinion from me but I don't agree with the strong emotional reaction against the anti-data-center movements that I've seen this week.

As I see it, algorithmic progress means that whatever you would be able to do with more and bigger data centers in 2…

— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) November 8, 2026

That movement had a big week. On November 3, voters in 10 states decided 41 local ballot measures on data centers, Ballotpedia counted. A “yes” vote on 28 of them would limit building through bans or moratoriums. After the vote, Senator Bernie Sanders called for a “national data center moratorium now,” one of several Democrats pushing to rein in the AI buildout.

Crypto’s AI corner has felt the same chill. Seven of the largest AI tokens fell 29.7% on average over the past 30 days, almost three times Bitcoin’s 10.7% drop.

So is the slowdown Buterin wants already showing up as a popping bubble in AI tokens?

His case rests on three points, and he made it, in his words, “without any controversial ‘doomer arguments’.”

He concluded that “a slowdown in compute hyper-scaling seems quite net good.” Even if it proved a mistake, it would not be worse than “10+ other political things,” he added.

The view fits what Buterin has argued since 2023, when he set out “d/acc,” his name for speeding up defensive technology first, in an essay titled My techno-optimism.

We compared the 30-day moves of seven of the largest AI tokens on Binance with Bitcoin and Ether.

The selling lines up with doubts about AI spending in the stock market. Last Thursday’s sell-off in chip stocks pushed Bitcoin below its 200-day average, and AI tokens, which rose fastest on the AI story, have fallen fastest as it cools.

A wave of local data center bans adds a new worry for tokens that sell computing power. Buterin’s own argument cuts the other way, though: if better algorithms keep AI improving on today’s machines, a slower buildout does not end demand for AI.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

It held on Sunday, but with little room to spare. Ether trades at $2,104 on Binance, down 16.1% in 30 days, after touching $2,060 late Sunday, its lowest price since August 19.

ETH sits below both of its daily exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that weight recent prices more. They stand at $2,311 for 200 days and $2,370 for 50 days.

For traders asking whether the crypto bubble is bursting, AI tokens are the place to watch. They rose fastest on the AI story, and they are now falling fastest.

With price currently trading at $1.096, XRP has already recorded another substantial drop. The market positioning of the asset remains weak, as XRP is trading below its major moving averages. Higher lows and fundamental improvements are two main priorities for the asset right now.

XRP's last bullish hope was a short recovery rally towards the $1.34 price threshold. It failed to hold on to that momentum and tumbled towards the area where buyers previously stopped the summer decline. From approximately $1.34, XRP lost roughly 18% of its value and lost everything it built up throughout the recovery.

But where would XRP finally settle down? Realistically, the closest support is the $1.075 level, matching the latest session's low, followed by the $1.03–$1.05 range and the $0.99–$1.00 area, both psychological and technical. A breakdown below, unfortunately, would put the summer bottom under pressure and open the way to further weakness.

But even if XRP is oversold, with RSI below 30, bulls might still stay sidelined. The XRP Ledger activated the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment on November 4. It removed an exploit that, under certain conditions, let accounts authorized to burn an issuer's tokens also mint them. The native supply of XRP has not been affected, luckily, but the amendment is not a factor that can help XRP reach key market levels.

In a case, where bulls somehow wake up, a recovery towards $1.15 and $1.20 is the main priority, while a proper trend reversal would require a move toward the moving averages around $1.30–$1.35.

Whether buyers can defend the $1 level or not is the main test for the asset right now. Without substantial volume, a short-lived price bounce here won't change the situation as a whole, unfortunately.

NEAR entered November under pressure after losing much of its September advance. After briefly reaching approximately $6 in October, the token fell toward $3.66 on November 9, according to the daily NEAR/USDT chart.

That represented a decline of roughly 39% from the local peak and put NEAR back at an important moving-average support zone.

Trading activity has also weakened alongside the price. Volume remains substantially below the levels seen during September’s breakout, suggesting that buyers have not yet returned with comparable strength.

However, lower volume does not necessarily confirm that selling pressure has disappeared. NEAR continues to form lower highs, while recovery attempts remain below its shorter-term moving averages.

Institutional exposure remains part of the investment case. Bitwise’s spot NEAR ETF, launched on September 29, held approximately 15.69 million NEAR worth $58.21 million as of Nov. 5. The fund reported that 99% of its holdings were staked.

Hyperliquid keeps going down and has recently violated an important moving average. It's now trading at $75, going further into downtrend, despite the strong fundamental background around Hyperliquid: Hyperliquid Strategies disclosure and a potential approval by the U.S. futures commission.

The broader market access, however, isn't something that the majority of retail investors consider a bullish catalyst, unfortunately. The asset has not yet found a strong bullish case. It's unlikely to be institutional too.

Technically, the bounce of HYPE/USDT could happen on 200 EMA, especially with a volume uptick and the recovery of the market in general. However, the selling pressure still overweights the buying support, according to exchange flows.

The netflow stays negative, and Hyperliquid is only yet to catch up with the bullish flow of the market. RSI confirms the thesis, moving around 40 and suggesting a bearish momentum, or a sideways movement at least. Volume should also surge substantially.

Key price levels for HYPE are: $72–$73 as the closest support level, $68 as the longer-term moving average, and $78–$80 as the first resistance level. Several moving averages sit at approximately $81–$85, so a breakthrough there should become a foundation for a price recovery.

Stellar already lost an important psychological level of $0.15, and there's a real scenario where XLM breaks down even more.

37% is the current recorded loss from its September peak of $0.235. The correction is rapidly erasing the recovery it has been building and finally invalidating it in October. The price is back in the accumulation range that was present back in May.

XLM moves below all major moving averages, with most of them aiming downwards and hinting at the aggravation of the current trend on the market.

With RSI and volume moving sideways or showing a descent, bear trend keeps the upper hand with sustained pressure on the price going further. The only positive signal could be the fact that RSI temporarily violated the reading of 30, which could be the sign of XLM approaching an oversold zone.

From a fundamental perspective, the Bell Protocol upgrade number 30 is the only thing that could set XLM apart from the rest of the market, with the vote scheduled for November 23.

The update will introduce: muxed contract addresses (ability to serve multiple users from a single smart contract), post-quantum signature verification and more.

In order to make the network more responsive, resilient and stronger in the future, millisecond ledger timing is also coming. It won't make the network faster on its own after the upgrade, but it opens up possibilities for developers to improve the network in the future.

The XRP rich list shows that accounts holding at least 10,000 XRP rank among the top 4% of the XRP Ledger. At the current price of around $1.10, this amount is worth approximately $11,000. Despite the number of accounts holding this amount increasing nearly sixfold since 2018, the threshold for entering the top 4% has remained close to 10,000 XRP throughout 2026.

The number of accounts holding at least 10,000 XRP has increased from 58,899 in May 2018 to approximately 342,000 currently.

Despite this growth, the amount needed to enter the top 4% has remained close to 10,000 XRP throughout 2026.

Historical data shows that the threshold was around 14,000 XRP in March 2020 and reached approximately 15,000 in January 2024 before declining.

The XRP Ledger has around 8.3 million accounts, with a median balance of approximately 20 XRP. This means half of all accounts hold 20 XRP or less.

XRP Scan identifies several large accounts belonging to exchanges and Ripple. Together, these accounts hold more than 40% of the XRP held by accounts with at least 10,000 XRP.

Coinbase is a notable example. Its labelled accounts collectively hold approximately 5.7 billion XRP, equivalent to around 574,000 holdings of 10,000 XRP each.

However, this does not represent the actual number of Coinbase customers holding that amount. Exchange accounts combine customer assets, and their individual balances are not publicly available.

Ripple also holds approximately 31 billion XRP in escrow, which is excluded from the regular account balances used in this comparison.

Santiment counted 2,147 wallets holding at least 1 million XRP, marking a 2026 high, according to reports from Bitcoin.com News and Crypto Briefing in early November.

XRP Scan showed 2,177 accounts with at least 1 million XRP on Monday, supporting a similar reading.

However, this remains below the 2,741 accounts recorded in July 2025, when XRP reached its record daily closing price.

At $1.10 per XRP, a 10,000-XRP holding is worth approximately $11,000. Every $0.10 change in XRP’s price changes the total value by $1,000.

At its record daily close of $3.55 on July 22, 2025, the holding was worth approximately $35,500. At $1.10, its value has fallen by nearly 69%.

Historical price movements show that XRP holders have faced lengthy recovery periods. After the January 2018 peak, XRP took approximately seven years to return to its previous price level in January 2025. Following the April 2021 peak, the recovery took around 3.6 years.

Interestingly, the number of accounts holding at least 10,000 XRP increased during both downturns. Between May 2018 and March 2020, the number grew from approximately 59,000 to 99,000, despite XRP’s price falling by around 83%.

The same trend continued during the 2021–2022 downturn, when the number of qualifying accounts more than doubled by January 2024. Since the July 2025 record, the group has grown by approximately 11%, even as XRP’s price declined by nearly two-thirds.

Historical comparisons offer both positive and negative signals.

When XRP previously traded at similar distances below its record price, it was higher one year later in approximately 64% of cases. The median return was around 21%, although more than one-third of those periods ended with lower prices.

Comparing XRP’s performance with the S&P 500, since November 5, 2024, XRP gained approximately 114%, while an S&P 500 fund gained around 30%, including dividends.

These figures reflect historical performance and do not guarantee future returns.

For now, three indicators remain important to watch: the number of accounts holding at least 1 million XRP, changes in the 10,000 XRP threshold for the top 4%, and XRP’s $1.10 price level.

Ultimately, holding 10,000 XRP places an account near the top 4% of the ledger, but it does not establish the same ranking among individual investors. The actual value of the holding will continue to depend on XRP’s market price.

#5236. Pompliano Says Bitcoin Spot ETFs Are Safer and More Convenient Than Hardware Wallets for Bitcoiners Holding Over $10,000

Pompliano’s comments on Bitcoin hardware wallets and Bitcoin ETFs come at a time when more people show interest in BTC amid security threats.

Bitcoin expert Anthony Pompliano today tackled a crucial question that serious Bitcoin investors often ask. The question is: between hardware wallets and ETFs, which one offers the best outcome for securing and getting exposure to Bitcoin?

In an interview released early today, the celebrated crypto analyst answered questions savvy investors want answered about Bitcoin self-custody versus Bitcoin ETFs.

Today, Bitcoin adoption grows at a remarkable rate. As more investors seek to invest in the cryptocurrency, there are two major ways to do so: gaining exposure through Bitcoin hardware wallets (self-custody) or Bitcoin ETFs.

In the podcast, Pompliano admitted that using spot ETFs is more secure than storing Bitcoin in a hardware wallet. According to the crypto expert, spot ETFs offer an accessible approach, providing investors with a simplified, regulated way to buy and invest in Bitcoin through their existing brokerage accounts. As Pompliano stated, ETFs stand out because they emphasize the importance of regulation in providing investor protection and market integrity.

Pompliano further recognized spot ETFs as the safest and the most convenient option for investors holding between $10,000 and $10 million worth of BTC. He said these investment vehicles offer greater liquidity than directly holding BTC on hardware wallets. They provide investors with diversified exposure to stock exchanges and on-chain markets.

However, he said convenience comes with caveats, as ETFs provide indirect exposure to Bitcoin. This means that investors don’t actually own the underlying Bitcoin. Also, ETFs might not provide investors with the same level of control as directly owning BTC in self-custody wallets.

This highlights the advantages of Bitcoin hardware wallets, which allow customers to hold BTC directly, giving them greater control. However, this level of control comes with the responsibility of managing private keys, asset control, and security risks.

The debate between self-custody and ETFs comes at a time when the crypto industry continues to experience increasing security breaches, with the latest and largest one being the Binance infiltration.

Such unfortunate hacking events compel customers to rethink how to secure their BTC while still accessing strong liquidity. The self-custody approach offers direct ownership and control of BTC, though it requires technical know-how and involves greater security risks. On the other hand, ETFs offer a simple, regulated way to gain exposure to the asset, with diversified liquidity. They, however, come with some limitations.

If XRP fails to react in the coming weeks, though, recovery will get “really, really difficult” for buyers. A confirmed bottom would need a strong five-leg rally above the first resistance.
